opportunities.title: Term Finance Got Governed to Death: How $8.5M Walked Out the Front Door of 'Decentralized' Voting
opportunities.why_now: An attacker didn't hack Term Finance's code — they just bought enough governance tokens to vote themselves the treasury, the same exploit pattern that's drained DAOs for years.
opportunities.angle: Post-mortem breakdown: timeline of the vote purchase, why token-weighted governance keeps failing, and a checklist for spotting vault protocols with this exact vulnerability

opportunities.title: BounceBit Isn't Fixing Its Chain — It's Fleeing to BNB After Getting Hit
opportunities.why_now: A $3M exploit was enough to make BounceBit abandon its own blockchain entirely rather than patch it, a rare public admission that some chains are unfixable once popped.
opportunities.angle: Sharp take/thread: what it means when a team chooses migration over remediation, and what that says about the actual security posture behind the marketing

opportunities.title: Coldcard's $130M Wake-Up Call: Your Hardware Wallet Was Never as Cold as You Thought
opportunities.why_now: A $130M exploit against a device marketed as the gold standard for self-custody is forcing new security measures — exactly the kind of story that should reset overconfidence in 'cold' storage.
opportunities.angle: Explainer: what actually broke, what the new measures fix (and don't), and a hard look at hardware wallet trust assumptions

opportunities.title: The Sandbox's Bridge Just Printed Free Money — Again, It Was a Bridge
opportunities.why_now: Attackers minted unbacked SAND across Base and BSC through a bridge exploit, the umpteenth reminder that cross-chain bridges remain crypto's weakest link even in 2026.
opportunities.angle: Pattern piece: log this alongside the year's other bridge exploits, make the case that 'contained' doesn't mean 'safe,' quick verdict on exposure

opportunities.title: MANTRA Halted Its Chain and Blamed Cosmos — Convenient Timing for a Network Built on Trust
opportunities.why_now: A chain-halt blamed on infrastructure rather than internal failure is a classic move worth scrutinizing, especially from a project that's had governance and trust issues before.
opportunities.angle: Skeptical breakdown: separate the technical claim from the accountability dodge, ask what 'blame the module' actually means for users with funds locked
